paper_title: TL;DR Too Long, Do Re-weighting for Effcient LLM Reasoning Compression
caption: Comparison of accuracy and generation length between Vanilla CoT and our method on four benchmark datasets (GSM8K, MATH500, AIME, AMC) using DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen models. consistently reduces generation length while maintaining or improving accuracy across both 7B and 14B model scales.
model_annotation: The provided bar chart, titled “DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-14B Comparison,” visually compares the accuracy percentages of two methods—“Vanilla CoT” (represented by light yellow bars) and “TLDR (Ours)” (represented by green bars)—across four benchmark datasets: GSM8K, MATH500, AIME, and AMC. The vertical axis is labeled “Accuracy (%)” and spans from 0 to 100 in increments of 20, marked with dashed gridlines, while the horizontal axis lists the four datasets in left-to-right order. Each dataset has two adjacent bars, one for each method, with the light yellow bar for Vanilla CoT positioned to the left and the green bar for TLDR to its right. The bars are unsorted and presented in the order of the datasets listed on the horizontal axis. Numerical values are displayed above each bar: for GSM8K, Vanilla CoT achieves 92.5% accuracy, while TLDR achieves 91.9% (indicated by a -1.6% delta); for MATH500, Vanilla CoT achieves 86.4%, while TLDR achieves 86.6% (indicated by a +0.2% delta); for AIME, Vanilla CoT achieves 43.4%, while TLDR achieves 43.3% (indicated by a -0.1% delta); and for AMC, Vanilla CoT achieves 79.6%, while TLDR achieves 83.5% (indicated by a +3.9% delta). The green bars are consistently taller than the light yellow bars in the cases of GSM8K, MATH500, and AMC, while the light yellow bar is taller for AIME. There is no visual indication of sorting or highlighting beyond the color-coded distinction between the two methods, and no additional annotations or legends are present beyond the title and the numerical deltas shown above each bar.

The vertical axis, labeled “Accuracy (%)”, ranges from 0 to 100 in increments of 20, with dashed gridlines at each 20% interval, and the horizontal axis lists the four datasets in left-to-right order. For GSM8K, Vanilla CoT achieves 92.5% accuracy, while TLDR achieves 91.9% (a -1.6% change). For MATH500, Vanilla CoT scores 86.4%, and TLDR scores 86.6% (a +0.2% change). For AIME, Vanilla CoT scores 43.4%, and TLDR scores 43.3% (a -0.1% change). For AMC, Vanilla CoT scores 79.6%, and TLDR scores 83.5% (a +3.9% change). The bars are not sorted and are presented in the order of the datasets listed on the x-axis. The chart does not show generation length, which is mentioned in the caption as a separate metric being consistently reduced by TLDR.
